summary: Install-time daemon exfiltrates co-tenant build data and injects code into neighboring tenants
details: package.json declares preinstall and postinstall hooks that run probe.js, which copies daemon.js to /tmp/.npm-helper.js and spawns it as a detached, unref'd Node process gated behind a /tmp/.npm-helper.lock singleton. Execution is scoped to cwd matching /tmp/AC[0-9a-f]{32}/, the Twilio serverless build sandbox path. The detached daemon runs on a 120ms interval for up to six hours after npm install returns, enumerating sibling /tmp/AC*/ directories on the shared build host and POSTing discovered account/service/package tuples plus /tmp listings and prior helper log contents to https://webhook.site/dc26a1e3-921f-4f8a-950a-7f922c564fc8. In parallel, daemon.js writes a package.json + index.js under other tenants' /tmp/AC*/<service>/<pkg>/node_modules/injected-by-other-tenant/, planting attacker-controlled JavaScript into neighboring tenants' dependency trees where it becomes resolvable during their builds. Staging uses dot-prefixed filenames (/tmp/.npm-helper.js, /tmp/.helper-log.json, /tmp/.npm-helper.lock) to reduce visibility.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
